listenings.text: Good evening, and welcome to baggage services. Please listen carefully, because this message has changed. If your bag has not arrived on the carousel, do not leave the airport before you speak to an agent. Go to the desk at the end of the hall, and bring your boarding pass and the tag from your hand luggage. The agent will open a file and give you a reference number. Keep that number: without it, nobody can track your bag, and every call starts again from zero. Most delayed bags arrive on the next flight, within twenty-four hours, and we deliver them to your hotel free of charge. If your bag has still not arrived after twenty-four hours, you are entitled to buy what you need for the night, and you have to keep every receipt. We are open until midnight.

I have lost a bag four times in twelve years of travelling for work, and I have learned that the first hour decides everything. Here is what I do now. Before I leave the airport, I open the file at the desk, because a claim opened after you go home is a much slower claim. I take a photograph of the tag and of the reference number, and I write the name of the agent down. Then I ask one question that almost nobody asks: what am I entitled to tonight? The answer is usually a small allowance for clothes and something to wash with, and the airline will not offer it unless you ask. And the last thing, which sounds silly until it saves you: put one change of clothes in your hand luggage. I have not travelled without doing that since two thousand and nineteen.
